channel.description: Posts in the discussion thread "Irish Fairies" - Irish Fairies, fay creatures that toy and manipulate with humans physically and mentally.

item.title: Re: Irish Fairies
item.content:encoded:
First of all, thanks for the crit. Secondly, multiple exploration logs/action scenarios would definitely work with the article, so I'll make sure to add that into the edit. One way I could structure it was this initial exploration log that reveals at least part of the SCP, a drone log that reveals the SCP's agency and malevolence, and a final action scenario that somehow contains the SCP (whether it be through neutralizing it or making a deal with it).

My main idea with the 'festival' was that the fairies have some sort of once in a millennium celebration that requires large amounts of humans to perform. I'm still deciding what exactly the festival's purpose is, but it's definitely not benevolent. Some of the ideas are a coronation of some monarch, a revival of some great being, or a way to connect two dimensions together. Again, those are just some of my ideas.

item.title: Re: Irish Fairies
item.content:encoded:
First of all, thanks for the crit, now let me explain some of my thought process

With the symmetrical hole, I really included that as a way for the Foundation to know something was off (rather than just a non-anomalous entity making people disappear), but you're right that I should tie it in at the end. I was mostly thinking of having actual fairies manipulate the situation rather than just fairy-like, so I could have a central fairy that speaks and talks to possibly one of MTF to show that it isn't just the forest being anomalous, but it's inhabitants. I also prefer having it be fairies rather than a fairy-like forest because it gives the SCP more agency rather than just 'spooky forest make bad things happen'.

A tale could work, to be honest, I was more biased towards an article because I'm more familiar with them compared to tales but I'll keep it in mind.

item.title: Re: Irish Fairies
item.content:encoded:
Gotta start off by saying, I’m generally a fan of all things fae (I mean, just look at my profile picture). So I like the idea of a fairy-based SCP. Though I’m noticing a few things here that I have to question.

First, what’s with the symmetrical hole? It just seems random and it’s never really explained. You seem to have such a consistent them with the traits later, and then there’s just this at the beginning. Second, is this actually fairies or is it just fairy-like? Either answer is fine but you want your reader to understand which it is. Because if I were reading this I’d think “cool, a forest that makes people go insane” not “there are probably creatures in that forest”. So if you actually want to be using fairies you should probably have some appear, but if you just want to use the traits of fairies and attribute them to a forest that’s also an option.

I’m going to throw out a suggestion, and keep in mind that you by no means have to take this. But you might want to write this as a tale. After all it doesn’t seem like you’re that interested in the containment of this anomaly. You didn’t even touch on that in your pitch. I could see a tale that was entirely devoted to the task force exploring this forest. It would give us more of a view into how they’re reacting to all the chaos happening around them. Again, I’m just throwing that out there. This can still work perfectly fine as a regular article.

item.title: Re: Irish Fairies
item.content:encoded:
Hey! Not a greenlighter, sorry.

So, your object itself is interesting enough- a nice cultural reference is generally good, and you also changed it up a little so that it wasn't just pulling straight from stories that already exist. Overall, the anomaly is solid enough, so that's good.

Your narrative is interesting. I enjoy the idea of a mysterious location like this one that represents a lot of danger for the Foundation, but if you leave it where you're leaving it now, the ending might be regarded as having too little detail. This seems like something that would be explored more than once, albeit with more appropriate gear the second time (for things like cognitohazards). Or, you could use drone exploration, if that would work. Really, I just think that you should either shine some light on this "festival" or at least provide some insight as to why they're saying "come to the festival." If you intend to leave the reader with a lot of questions, you should get them a little closer to their answers so that they can infer details, rather than leaving it completely vague.

This type of object seems like the kind of thing that the Foundation is going to have a hard time containing- a sort of "neutralize the threat by any means" type of scenario. Do you plan on expanding on that through the narrative? That would definitely involve more exploration logs/action scenarios and stuff along those lines. I recommend including those types of things if that's the storyline you want to use, but if these are easy to contain, then I would instead suggest controlled experiments and research logs. In the end, though, you should do whatever you feel is best for the article and go from there- these are just suggestions.

Overall, the concept looks good. Try to get some additional advice on how to develop this narrative if you feel like you need it. I hope I was able to help. Good luck developing your idea!

item.title: Irish Fairies
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: No.

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror

Elevator Pitch: The basic idea is that the SCPs are based on Irish fairies, who are (in short) tricksters who manipulate humans in various ways. Whether that be by manipulating their mind to go crazy or manipulating their body to disform them. Fairies were blamed for various things in medieval Ireland, some of those include stuff like schizophrenia or disabilities being 'curses' from fairies. The SCP will differ from generic fairies by being inherently malevolent when the original fairies are not.

Central Narrative: After various missing person reports, and the discovery of a body missing a symmetrical hole in their chest, the Foundation investigate a forest in Ireland. While investigating, one of the team starts hearing voices telling them to kill their teammates and to 'come to the festival' upon telling the team of this the MTF, assuming the SCP has something to do with this, detain and amnestisize the teammate. They leave one MTF to bring the affected teammate out of the forest to safety and continue. After a bit, the MTF see various colorful lights in the distance, and they all begin to hear voices telling them to 'come to the festival'. At this point, the MTF stop broadcasting their video and we are left with only their audio. The captian, who appears to be the least affected, descibes what's happening while the others start going mad. Eventually the captian attempts to flee the situation at which various ereathral screaming can be heard before he goes offline.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Well I tried my best to make sure it leaves a lot of questions, and the fact that it's a twist on what is normally considered cute or harmless is pretty interesting.

Additional Notes: I don't know how I feel about the narrative (which is why I'm not seeking a greenlight yet), so I would like critisicm to be focused on that.
